reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the key premises regarding improved CO oxidation activity, lower light-off temperature, and enhanced durability for a 7-metal HESO compared to a 4-metal MESO under dry, lean conditions. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a system with additionally dispersed Pt-group metals, a specific mechanism involving oxygen vacancies and electronic conductivity, and a predicted 60% reduction in light-off temperature, none of which are directly supported by E1.
premises: High configurational entropy in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity under dry, lean conditions.
A 7-metal high-entropy spinel oxide (HESO) shows a 63% lower T10 for CO oxidation vs. a 4-metal spinel (MESO).
The 7-metal HESO exhibits better long-term stability (4.7% vs. 12.2% activity decrease over 14 h) than the 4-metal MESO.
The homogeneous multi-element distribution in HESO is confirmed by structural characterization.
